sweep_summary: Three title-hits for nama1264. (1) Selting 1995 is a false Glottolog language assignment (record says 'computerized assignment from gesprach'); it is a book on German conversational prosody — irrelevant, not fetched sources. (2) Kusmer 2019 (already on file, re-read) is about tone sandhi and prosodic displacement; silent on word stress. (3) Brugman 2009, fetched sources open from Cornell eCommons (hdl 1813/13921, 321 pp., saved with extracted text), is the key find: p.28 'Khoekhoe lacks both stress and segmental alternations' and p.88 'Khoekhoe has no stress, segment or tone alternations' — a first-hand, fieldwork-based statement that CONTRADICTS the catalog's fixed-strict (initial) coding, which currently has no located source text and rests on Gordon 2002's appendix line 'Initial (mora)' (via Hagman 1977). Earlier files on file add Hahn 1870 §8 p.24 (accent on the monosyllabic stem = first syllable) and Planert 1905 p.109 (stress sometimes on stem, sometimes on suffix; 'Die Ansicht Fr. Müllers über die Betonung ist also nicht richtig'). Net: sources conflict; the best modern statement is 'no stress'. Still unread and worth acquiring: Hagman 1977 Nama Hottentot grammar (print only; Google Books API 0 items, HathiTrust catalog behind Cloudflare, archive.org 0 hits) — high priority as the StressTyp2/Gordon source; Beach 1938 and Haacke 1999 tonology medium. Receipts in and.

new_statements.locator: p.28 (PDF p.52), §3.0; corroborated p.88 (PDF p.112): 'Unfortunately, Khoekhoe has no stress, segment or tone alternations to shed light on the question.'
new_statements.reading: A modern, fieldwork-based phonological study states outright that Khoekhoe (Nama) has no word stress; word-level prominence is tonal (six citation melodies, left-aligned) and structural (bimoraic root = head foot), not metrical stress. This is the first explicit first-hand statement on the question read for this language and it contradicts the catalog's fixed-strict initial coding. It also conflicts with Hahn 1870 §8 p.24 ('Der Accent bleibt auf der Stammsilbe... stets auf der ersten Silbe'), an 1870 statement whose 'Accent' sits beside a three-way tone description (§7), and Planert 1905 p.109 already contradicted Hahn ('betont bald die Stammsilbe, bald das Suffix'). The catalog entry should move from fixed-strict to at least 'descriptions disagree', and to NO-WORD-STRESS/TONAL if Hagman 1977 (unread; the Gordon 2002 source) does not give an explicit stress rule.

sources.quote: 'Der Accent bleibt auf der Stammsilbe, und, da ... alle Staemme des Wortes im Hottentotischen monosyllabisch sind, stets auf der ersten Silbe. Bei Compositen aus Stoffwoertern faellt der Ton dagegen auf diejenige erste Silbe der Wurzel, welche den Begriff des zusammengesetzten Wortes hauptsaechlich bestimmt ... In reduplicirten Staemmen hat in der Regel die erste Silbe den Ton ...; tritt jedoch ein adjectivisches oder adverbiales Suffix an ... so geht der Ton auf die zweite Silbe ueber' (sec. 7 same page describes three lexical tones).

sources.quote: Hagman (1977) is a general descriptive grammar; Haacke (1976) provides detailed studies of the nominal domain, while Haacke (1999) gives an overview of the tonology. On the analytic side, Brugman (2009) provides a detailed look at the phonetics and phonology of tone in Khoekhoe.
sources.locator: ch. 5 'Khoekhoe tone sandhi' (diss. p.60ff.); ch.1 fn on sources
sources.note: Full text on file (6900+ lines) re-grepped this sweep: every occurrence of 'stress'/'accent' concerns Irish, English or other languages (e.g. 'In Irish, some unstressed pronouns may be postposed'). Khoekhoe is treated as a tone language with phrase-level tone sandhi and mora-based particle weight ('preverbal particles are at most one mora, while postverbal particles are at least two'); no statement about Khoekhoe word stress anywhere. Silent on word stress.
